task: Native sparse raw-KV access concentration, not predictive hit rate
text_source: PG19 test, identical document prefixes with model-specific tokenization
placement_unit: one request/layer/64-token block including all KV heads
primary_metric: For each query, union native selected historical block IDs across heads/groups; one count per query and block
secondary_metric: Native per-group selector occurrences; not physical memory transactions
ranking: Retrospective per-document, per-layer, within the same evaluation window
averaging: Equal layer mean within document, then equal mean over three documents; document min/max
native_budgets: Unmodified public checkpoint selector configuration; fixed sink/local blocks included
nosa_source: Causally crop query positions [32256,32768) from existing complete 33280-token native traces
nsa_scope: Raw/main KV selection including sink/local; compressed KV branch state reported separately
limitations: Three long literary documents are diagnostic, not an agent-workload benchmark
Full causal prefill selection traces, not a decode latency experiment
Retrospective ranking does not establish advance predictability
Raw block selection frequency is neither attention mass nor physical HBM traffic
Different native selector budgets and architectures are preserved
